figures.caption: Fig. 3. Effect of a single fault injection with a fault length of three on the training loss and the parameter update magnitude Rt. The injected fault triggers a sharp spike in Rt, after which the training loss exhibits a bump before gradually stabilizing at a slightly elevated level. This example illustrates how gradient corruption propagates through the optimizer and leads to harmful parameter updates.

Fig. 4. Effect of the detector sensitivity parameter α on recomputation behavior over 2,000 training steps for the 60M-parameter model. Results are shown per bit position and averaged across all bit positions (in black). Left: Recompute precision, indicating how often recomputation corresponds to true corruption. Increasing α raises the false alarm rate, leading to unnecessary recomputation. Center: Detection rate, showing increased sensitivity as α increases. Right: Evaluation loss, which exhibits an increase for smaller α relative to the baseline variation (3.881± 0.002, after 2,000 steps).

Fig. 1. Evaluation loss, parameter difference, gradient norm before clipping, and maximum attention logits for different bit positions and kernels (FPi and BPi, referring to the i-th GEMM kernel in the forward or backward pass, respectively). Evaluation loss and parameter difference represent the value observed after the training span. The gradient norm and the maximum attention logits represent the maximum values observed over the training span.
